proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a cohort \(s\) and condition on \((E_0,\widetilde z_s=z)\).  By \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, this conditioning does not change the conditional historical-design law.  Define
\[
\ell_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h),\qquad
\Phi_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)^\top.
\]
Bounded support of \(K\), the density bounds, and a change of variables give constants \(0<c_0<C_0<\infty\), uniform in \(s,t,z,h\), such that
\[
c_0h^d\le \mathbb E[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0]\le C_0h^d,
\quad
\mathbb E[v^\top\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v\mid E_0]\ge c_0h^d
\]
for every unit vector \(v\).  The lower matrix bound follows because \(K\) is bounded below near zero, every truncated cube contains a fixed orthant box, and a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish almost everywhere on such a box.  Compactness of the unit sphere makes the lower constant uniform.  Choose \(c_G<c_0/(4C_0)\).

Let \(b_T=\lceil C_\beta\log(T\vee2)\rceil\).  The geometric mixing premise permits \(C_\beta\) such that \(T\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\le T^{-A}\).  Divide the calendar into blocks of length at most \(b_T\) and split them into odd and even families.  Successively replacing each separated block by an independent copy changes either parity law in total variation by at most
\[
C(T/b_T)\beta_P(b_T\mid E_0)\le CT^{-A}.
\]
For either \(F=\ell_{z,h}\) or \(F=v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\), a block sum \(W_g\) satisfies \(0\le W_g\le Cb_T\) and \(W_g^2\le Cb_TW_g\).  Under the coupled product law,
\[
\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(W_g)\le Cb_TTh^d.
\]
Expansion of the exponential series for the centered block sums, followed by exponential Markov optimization, therefore yields
\[
P\left(\left|\sum_{t=1}^T\{F(X_{st})-\mathbb EF(X_{st})\}\right|>cTh^d
\,\middle|\,E_0,z\right)
\le C\exp\{-cTh^d/b_T\}+CT^{-A}.
\tag{1}
\]
Apply \((1)\) to the mass and to quadratic forms on a fixed \(1/4\)-net of the unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^{q_r}\).  Since \(q_r\) is fixed and
\(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\max_v|v^\top Av|\) on that net, outside the probability in \((1)\) the calendar mass is at most \(2C_0Th^d\) and the calendar Gram matrix is at least \((c_0/2)Th^dI\).  Replication multiplies both by \(n_s\), so the normalized-shape test succeeds.  Hence
\[
P\{\text{candidate }h\text{ fails}\mid E_0,z\}
\le C\exp\{-cTh^d/b_T\}+CT^{-A}.
\tag{2}
\]

Put \(h_0=h_{s,\beta}\).  Its log-spacing component and sufficiently large \(C_h\) imply
\[
T(2^vh_0)^d/b_T\ge c2^{vd}.
\]
If selection has not stopped by \(2^vh_0\), that candidate failed; substituting into \((2)\) proves the asserted dyadic tail.  At \(h=1\), \((2)\) gives the terminal bound.  Summation by tails gives, for fixed \(a>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E[(h_s)^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,z]
&\le h_0^a+\sum_{v:2^vh_0<1}(2^{v+1}h_0)^aP(h_s>2^vh_0\mid E_0,z)\\
&\le Ch_0^a+CT^{-A_a}\\
&\le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}+
\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)^{a/d}+N^{-a/2}\right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the coupling exponent may be chosen as \(A_a>a/d+2\) and \(\sum_v2^{av}e^{-c2^{vd}}<\infty\).  A union bound over fixed \(S\), the terminal estimate, and \(\delta_N=O(N^{-1/2})\) imply \(P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\).  Finally \(Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2)\) directly from its definition, even when the uninflated smoothing count is bounded.  This proves the lemma without an outcome-mixing or upper-mass condition.

Put \(D=Sd\) and define in this proof \(Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0)\).  The definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\) give
\[
\mathbb E[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]=D.
\]
Jensen's inequality and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} yield
\[
D^2\le \mathbb E[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le B.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \(B<D^2\) makes the class empty.

Fix any admissible interior query \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\); the following construction is repeated pointwise over that region, and its conditional event-state law puts probability one on the selected query, hence at least \(c_X\).  For every compatible \(B\ge D^2\), the non-donor channels use the common donor law
\[
Z_j=z_0+U_j,\qquad U_j\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{\pm\sqrt D e_k:1\le k\le D\}.
\]
It has mean zero around \(z_0\), covariance \(I_D\), and fourth moment \(D^2\).  Draw event outcomes independently of the complete design and draw bounded historical response paths independently across units conditional on that design, with conditional mean \(m_s(X_{st})\).  Complete untreated event outcomes to have cohort-average mean \(m_s(z_{0s})\), impose consistency, no spillovers, and limited anticipation, and set the recorded paths equal to the exact paths.  This verifies the causal and full-design centering restrictions.

For the treated channel, let \(V=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\) and perturb the event-response probability in cohort \(s\) by
\[
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV^{1/2}}.
\]
Then \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\), the squared target separation is \(cV\) by \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, and the binary relative-entropy bound on probabilities bounded away from zero and one gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)\le C\sum_sn_sv_s^2\le Cc_0^2.
\tag{4}
\]
For smoothing, choose a cohort maximizing its summand in \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\), put \(b=c_b(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\), and add the Holder bump \(c_1b^\lambda\psi((x-z_{0s})/b)\).  A fixed affine carrier for \(\lambda>1\), or an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier for \(\lambda\le1\), chosen inside the two-sided-modulus envelope, preserves that envelope for small \(c_1\).  The squared target separation is at least \(cR_{\mathrm{sm}}\), while density bounds and conditional product response kernels give
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)\le CTn_sb^{2\lambda+d}\le C.
\tag{5}
\]
The established spacing lemma supplies the beta-mixing pair, its positive affinity, and separation \(cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\).

For the donor channel assume the fixed slack \(B-D^2>0\).  Choose \(0<\xi<D\) with \(D^2+\xi^2<B\), set \(r_\pm=(D\pm\xi)^{1/2}\), and use the common support \(z^{(0)}\pm r_-e_k,z^{(0)}\pm r_+e_k\).  Give every atom mass \(1/(4D)\) under law zero.  For \(\mu=c_2N^{-1/2}\), alter the four masses in direction \(e_1\) by
\[
-b_N/2+a_N,\quad -b_N/2-a_N,\quad b_N/2,\quad b_N/2,
\qquad a_N=\mu/(2r_-),\quad b_N=\mu^2/(2\xi).
\]
They remain positive for small fixed \(c_2\).  Direct summation gives means \(z^{(0)}\) and \(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\mu e_1\), covariance \(I_D\) under both laws, and baseline fourth moment \(D^2+\xi^2<B\).  Continuity of the finite-support moment and the fixed slack keep the second moment below \(B\).  The product donor divergence is at most \(CN(a_N^2+b_N^2)\le Cc_2^2\).  A nonzero affine slope when \(\kappa=1\), or unequal positive cusps centered at the two query points when \(\kappa<1\), gives target separation at least \(c\mu^\kappa\), hence squared separation \(cN^{-\kappa}\), while preserving the local modulus after fixed rescaling.

Finally, if \(\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)\le\eta\), the log-sum inequality and the binary bound \(\operatorname{kl}(p,q)\ge2(p-q)^2\) imply
\[
\int\min(dP_0,dP_1)=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\sqrt{\eta/2}.
\]
Choosing the perturbation constants small gives positive affinity in (4), (5), and the donor channel; the spacing lemma supplies it directly.  The causal completion above proves membership.  At \(B=D^2\), the common donor law remains valid for treated, smoothing, and spacing, but the strict-slack perturbation is unavailable, so no donor converse is asserted.

The emptiness assertion follows from equation \((3)\) in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}.  If \(B>D^2\), apply that lemma to each of the four channels.  If the channel targets are \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), their difference is \(\Delta_q\), and their affinity is \(A_q>0\), then for every estimator the two events
\[
\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space.  Integration against the overlap measure yields
\[
\max_{\ell=0,1}\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}
[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge A_q\Delta_q^2/8\ge cR_q.
\tag{6}
\]
Maximizing over all four channels proves the strict-slack lower bound.  At \(B=D^2\), the lemma supplies (6) only for treated, smoothing, and beta-spacing, which proves exactly the stated boundary lower bound.

For the upper bound condition on the complete historical design, \(E_0\), and all donors.  On successful fits, identification and the local-polynomial linear representation give
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{7}
\]
The two full-design restrictions center the first two terms under this conditioning.  Conditional cross-unit independence, boundedness, and \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} give
\[
\mathbb E[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\cdot]\le B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\qquad
\mathbb E[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\cdot]
\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{8}
\]
The Holder Taylor remainder and kernel support give
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
The beta-mixing selector lemma with exponent \(2\lambda\) therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{9}
\]

Let \(Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\) and \(W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_jY_j\).  Independence, centering, and covariance identity imply, by expanding the fourth power and retaining the all-equal and paired indices,
\[
\mathbb E\|W_N\|_2^4
\le \frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\tag{10}
\]
Projection and ellipticity imply
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2.
\]
The upper modulus on the local event, boundedness on its complement, Lyapunov's inequality, Markov's inequality, and (10) yield
\[
\mathbb E[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]\le CN^{-\kappa}.
\tag{11}
\]
On the bad sample the squared error is bounded because the target is in \([-B,B]\) and the deterministic absolute-weight bound controls successful intercepts.  The selector lemma makes its contribution \(O(R_{\star,\beta})\).  Squaring (7), then using (8)--(11), proves the estimator upper bound.  Since the estimator is measurable and uses no unknown covariance, it also upper-bounds the minimax infimum.  This completes both compatible cases.

Put \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\) and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N)\).  On a successful fit, polynomial reproduction and the Holder Taylor remainder give
\[
\left|\widehat m_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t,i}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{12}
\]
After weighting, the right side is \(A_L\).

Define \(\mathsf H_{si}=\pi_s\sum_ta_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\).  Historical full-design centering and donor independence center these variables under the displayed conditioning, while cross-unit independence makes them independent over \((s,i)\).  Their conditional range lengths are at most \(B\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|\).  Hoeffding's exponential-moment argument, obtained from convexity of the exponential on each bounded range, gives
\[
P\left(\left|\sum_{s,i}\mathsf H_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}\,middle|\,
\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{13}
\]
Likewise the variables
\[
\mathsf E_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}
\]
are conditionally centered by event full-design stability, are independent across units, and have range lengths \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  Hence
\[
P\left(\left|\sum_{s,i}\mathsf E_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}\,middle|\,
\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right)\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{14}
\]

With \(W_N\) as in (10), Markov's inequality gives
\[
P\{\|W_N\|_2>q_N\mid E_0\}
\le M_4(N)/q_N^4=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{15}
\]
On the complementary donor event, projection and ellipticity bound the standardized displacement by \(\delta_N\).  On the good sample \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\), so the upper local modulus gives donor error at most \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  On the bad sample the fallback interval \([-B,B]\) contains the target.  On the intersection of the good and donor events, identification, (12), and the donor bound show that noncoverage implies (13) or (14).  Bonferroni and iterated conditioning therefore give
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha.
\tag{16}
\]
This is finite-sample and no selector probability enters it.

For length, the deterministic weight lemma gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}+R_{\mathrm{evt}}\le CR_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\qquad
A_L\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
The beta selector moment with exponent \(\lambda\) and fixed \(S\) yields
\[
\mathbb E[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\},
\]
and the donor formula gives \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}\).  The fallback length is at most \(2B\), and the selector bad probability is \(O(R_{\star,\beta})\).  Thus
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{17}
\]

For a lower pair with affinity \(A_q>2\alpha+a_0\), honesty and the overlap measure \(P_0\wedge P_1\) imply
\[
(P_0\wedge P_1)\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\]
On this event the interval length is at least \(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\), whence
\[
\max_{\ell=0,1}\mathbb E_{P_\ell}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{18}
\]
The perturbation constants in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} may be fixed sufficiently small to make every available affinity exceed \(2\alpha+a_0\).  Maximizing (18) over four channels when \(B>D^2\), and over exactly the three non-donor channels when \(B=D^2\), proves the two lower bounds.  Replacing \(\alpha\) by \(\alpha+\epsilon\) and then taking fixed small \(\epsilon\) proves the asymptotically honest version.  Equations (16)--(18) prove the theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(h_s^{\mathrm{iid}}\) be selected from the dyadic grid starting at \(h_{s,\mathrm{iid}}\) in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  For a sufficiently large fixed \(C_h\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\), every cohort and every integer \(v\ge0\) with \(2^vh_{s,\mathrm{iid}}\le1\) satisfy
\[
P\{h_s^{\mathrm{iid}}>2^vh_{s,\mathrm{iid}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp(-c2^{vd}).
\]
For every fixed \(a>0\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[(h_s^{\mathrm{iid}})^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good,iid}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s]
\le C\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}+T^{-a/d}+N^{-a/2}\}.
\]
The terminal-grid failure probability is at most \(C\exp(-cT)\), and the iid bad-sample probability is at most \(CR_\star\) along arrays with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\).  No logarithmic block length, dense-local-site condition, or upper local-mass condition is used.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Condition on \((E_0,\widetilde z_s=z)\).  Donor independence preserves the historical-design law, and the subclass definition makes the calendar vectors independent.  For \(\ell_{z,h}\) and \(\Phi_{z,h}\) defined in the beta-selector proof, the same density, kernel, cube-geometry, and polynomial arguments give
\[
c_0h^d\le\mathbb E\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\le C_0h^d,
\qquad
\mathbb E[v^\top\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v]\ge c_0h^d
\]
uniformly over unit vectors \(v\).  Each summand is bounded and its variance is at most \(Ch^d\).  For a centered bounded variable \(V\), expansion of the exponential series gives
\[
\mathbb Ee^{\theta V}
\le\exp\left\{\frac{\theta^2\operatorname{Var}(V)}{2(1-C|\theta|)}\right\}
\]
for sufficiently small \(|\theta|\).  Multiplication over the independent calendar indices and exponential Markov optimization yield
\[
P\left(\left|\sum_{t=1}^T\{F(X_{st})-\mathbb EF(X_{st})\}\right|>cTh^d
\,\middle|\,E_0,z\right)\le C\exp(-cTh^d)
\tag{19}
\]
for \(F=\ell_{z,h}\) and for every fixed quadratic form of \(\Phi_{z,h}\).  A fixed sphere net turns (19) into simultaneous mass and Gram bounds.  Replication cancels from \(G_s/L_s\), so
\[
P\{\text{candidate }h\text{ fails}\mid E_0,z\}
\le C\exp(-cTh^d).
\tag{20}
\]

Put \(h_0=h_{s,\mathrm{iid}}\).  The term \(T^{-1/d}\) ensures
\[
T(2^vh_0)^d\ge c2^{vd}.
\]
If the selector has not stopped by \(2^vh_0\), that candidate failed, so (20) gives the stated tail; setting \(h=1\) gives \(Ce^{-cT}\).  Tail summation and \(\sum_v2^{av}e^{-c2^{vd}}<\infty\) give
\[
\mathbb E[(h_s^{\mathrm{iid}})^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good,iid}}\mid E_0,z]
\le Ch_0^a
\le C\{(Tn_s)^{-a/(2\lambda+d)}+T^{-a/d}+N^{-a/2}\}.
\]
A union bound over fixed \(S\), \(e^{-cT}\le CT^{-2\lambda/d}\), and the deterministic eventual inequality \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\) prove the bad-event bound by \(CR_\star\).  This proves every claim directly from independent bounded concentration.

added_lemmas.statement: Put \(D=Sd\).  For every fixed nonempty independent-calendar class with \(B>D^2\), each of the four rates \(R_{\mathrm{tr}},R_{\mathrm{sm}},R_{\mathrm{sp}},R_{\mathrm{don}}\) has a two-law subexperiment contained in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\), with conditional testing affinity uniformly bounded away from zero and squared target separation bounded below by a fixed positive multiple of that rate.  The treated, smoothing, and donor pairs may be chosen with bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence.  The iid spacing pair uses independent uniform calendar designs and a query neighborhood of volume proportional to \(T^{-1}\); its no-hit event has probability bounded away from zero and its target separation is of order \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).  At \(B=D^2\), the same assertions hold only for \(R_{\mathrm{tr}},R_{\mathrm{sm}},R_{\mathrm{sp}}\), using a common donor marginal; no universal donor converse is asserted.  If \(B<D^2\), the class is empty.  Every pair is completed as a regular conditional law of the complete causal panel and obeys both full-design centering restrictions.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The compatibility calculation in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} gives emptiness for \(B<D^2\) and supplies bounded causal response kernels, admissible surfaces, event completions, and donor laws for the treated, smoothing, and donor perturbations.  Choose the historical stacked calendar vectors in those constructions independently with the uniform density on \([0,1]^{Sd}\).  This density satisfies \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), is geometrically beta mixing with coefficient zero, and is conditionally independent across calendar indices.  Draw the bounded historical responses conditionally on the full design, independently across units, with means \(m_s(X_{st})\), and draw event outcomes independently of the design.  Thus the full-design centering restrictions and every causal completion used by the established embedding remain valid.  The treated and donor likelihood ratios do not involve the historical design.  For the smoothing bump of radius \(b=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\), uniform design gives hit probability \(O(b^d)\), so the established binary likelihood calculation remains
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)\le CTn_sb^{2\lambda+d}\le C.
\]
Consequently the treated, smoothing, and, under fixed strict donor slack, donor pairs belong to the iid subclass with their stated separations.  The common spherical donor law from the established embedding proves the same assertion for the two non-donor channels at \(B=D^2\).

It remains to build iid spacing.  Fix an admissible interior query \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\).  Let \(b=c_bT^{-1/d}\) and let \(A_b\) be an interior cube centered at one cohort query block, of side proportional to \(b\), so that \(|A_b|=c/T\).  Under both laws draw all calendar vectors independently and uniformly.  Then
\[
P\{X_{s_*t}\notin A_b\text{ for every }t\mid E_0\}
=(1-c/T)^T\ge a>0
\tag{21}
\]
after decreasing the fixed \(c\), uniformly in \(T\), with finitely many small \(T\) absorbed into \(a\).  Start from an admissible affine carrier when \(\lambda>1\), or asymmetric Holder-cusp carrier when \(\lambda\le1\), and perturb one cohort surface by \(c_1b^\lambda\psi((x-z_{0s_*})/b)\), with compact support inside \(A_b\) and \(\psi(0)=1\).  A sufficiently small fixed \(c_1\) preserves boundedness, the Holder ball, and both sides of the local modulus.  Complete untreated event outcomes according to event transport while keeping the observed event mean fixed.  Identification then gives
\[
|\tau_{n,P_1}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_0}(z_0)|ge cb^\lambda=cT^{-\lambda/d}.
\tag{22}
\]
On the no-hit event in (21), every observed historical response kernel is identical under the two laws, and the event and donor observed laws were chosen identical.  Hence the restrictions of the two observed-data laws to that event coincide, so their affinity is at least \(a\).  Equations (21)--(22) prove the spacing claim.  The common spherical donor distribution has covariance \(I_D\) and fourth moment \(D^2\), so this construction also works at the boundary.  Together with the first paragraph, this proves every asserted iid channel and the exact envelope split.

added_lemmas.statement:
Put \(D=Sd\).  For each fixed nonempty independent-calendar class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\) with \(B>D^2\), along every array with \(N\wedge T\wedge\min_s n_s\to\infty\), uniformly for almost every admissible realized path \(z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), allowed to depend on the fixed slack \(B-D^2\), such that
\[
cR_\star\le
\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{iid}}-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_\star.
\]
At \(B=D^2\), the same iid-tuned estimator has risk at most \(CR_\star\), while the universal lower bound is only \(c(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}})\); no donor converse is asserted.  At \(B<D^2\) the class is empty.  Thus conditional calendar independence removes the logarithm from the spacing channel without changing the treated, smoothing, or generated-donor terms.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Apply the two-point squared-error argument in equation \((6)\) to the four iid pairs in \texttt{lem:iid-joint-law-embedding}.  This gives the \(R_\star\) lower bound under strict slack.  At equality apply it to exactly the three available non-donor pairs, yielding the stated boundary lower bound.

For the upper bound, repeat decomposition \((7)\) for \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{iid}}\).  Equations \((8)\), based only on full-design centering, cross-unit independence, boundedness, and deterministic local-polynomial weights, are unchanged.  The iid selector moment with exponent \(2\lambda\) replaces (9) by
\[
\mathbb E[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good,iid}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}+T^{-2\lambda/d}+N^{-\lambda}\}
\le CR_\star.
\]
The donor calculation (10)--(11) is unchanged because the same full donor mean and projection are used, and it gives \(CN^{-\kappa}\).  The iid selector bad-event probability is \(O(R_\star)\), while the error is uniformly bounded there.  Squaring the four-term decomposition gives the upper bound.  The estimator is observed-data measurable and does not use \(\Sigma\), completing the minimax bracket and boundary qualification.

The conditional coverage proof (12)--(16) depends only on polynomial reproduction, Holder bias, bounded unit clusters, the two full-design centering restrictions, cross-unit independence, donor independence, the donor fourth-moment calculation, ellipticity, and the upper local modulus.  Every one of these premises holds in the iid subclass, and \(C_{\alpha,\mathrm{iid}}\) uses exactly the same radii and fallback computed from its own weights.  Replacing each selected beta bandwidth by \(h_s^{\mathrm{iid}}\) in (12)--(16) therefore proves exact finite-sample coverage.

prose_updates.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and explain why compounded buy-and-hold wealth requires more than linear return matching. Barber and Lyon (1997) and Mitchell and Stafford (2000) likewise motivate attention to dependence and compounding in long-horizon returns. Matching only marginal or mean return paths generally discards within-path dependence needed for compounded wealth; this is motivation, not a theorem or an observational-equivalence claim under the maintained full wealth panel. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates, while Gaiffas (2007) provides a pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), and Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study different generated-coordinate or measurement-error experiments. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest beta-mixing block-coupling template, and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. The banked predecessor proves a no-log proxy-modulus result only in its fixed-query conditional experiment. The new result lifts that phenomenon to the present complete causal panel class, supplies a feasible estimator and honest interval, and proves the independent-calendar frontier for every \(\lambda>0\), alongside the distinct log-spacing frontier under design-only geometric beta mixing.

proofs.proof_tex:
Set
\[
a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d},
\qquad
q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}.
\]
The declared conditions \(\lambda>0\) and \(d>0\) imply \(a\in(0,1)\) and \(q>0\).  We first prove the only inequality needed for the rate reduction.  For \(u>0\), let
\[
\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a.
\]
Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
\phi'(u)=a\bigl(1-u^{a-1}\bigr).
\]
Because \(a-1<0\), the derivative is negative on \((0,1)\) and positive on \((1,\infty)\).  Thus \(u=1\) is a global minimizer, so \(\phi(u)\geq0\).  Substitution of \(u=x/y\), followed by multiplication by \(y>0\), gives
\[
x^ay^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
\qquad x>0,\qquad y>0.
\tag{1}
\]
Moreover,
\[
q(1-a)
=\frac{2\lambda}{d}\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}
=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
=a.
\tag{2}
\]
For each cohort \(s\), positivity of the integers \(T\) and \(n_s\) permits (1) to be applied with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\).  By (2),
\[
\begin{aligned}
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
&=n_s^{-a}T^{-a}\\
&=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}\\
&\leq an_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The cohort-weight conditions in the frozen symbol declaration give \(\pi_s>0\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s=1\).  Hence
\[
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2
\leq\left(\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\right)^2
=1.
\tag{4}
\]
Multiplying (3) by \(\pi_s^2\), summing over \(s\), applying (4), and using the definitions of \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\), we obtain
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\tag{5}
\]

For every positive integer \(T\), one has \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\).  Since \(q>0\), the definition of \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) gives
\[
T^{-q}
\leq(\log2)^{-q}
\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
=(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (5) and (6) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
&\leq\{a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)\\
&=C_{\lambda,d}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Here the second line uses \(cx+dy\leq(c+d)(x\vee y)\) for nonnegative \(c,d,x,y\), and the last line uses \(1-a=d/(2\lambda+d)\) and \(q=2\lambda/d\).  Since \(0<\log2<1\) and \(q>0\),
\[
C_{\lambda,d}=a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\geq a+(1-a)=1.
\tag{8}
\]
Define
\[
A_\beta:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\qquad
D_\beta:=A_\beta\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
All rate components are positive by \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\).  Its definition of \(R_{\star,\beta}\), together with (7)--(8), gives
\[
D_\beta
\leq R_{\star,\beta}
=D_\beta\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq D_\beta\vee(C_{\lambda,d}A_\beta)
\leq C_{\lambda,d}D_\beta.
\tag{9}
\]
This proves the asserted uniform comparison with constants \(1\) and \(C_{\lambda,d}\).

If \(T\geq3\), then \(T\vee2=T\) and \(\log T\geq\log3>1\), so
\[
T^{-q}\leq\left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right)^q
=R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{10}
\]
Substituting (10) into (5) and using \(a\in(0,1)\) gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{11}
\]
Taking the maximum with \(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\), \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), and \(R_{\mathrm{don}}\) in the definition of \(R_{\star,\beta}\) proves
\[
R_{\star,\beta}=A_\beta\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{12}
\]

For the independent-calendar subclass in \(\texttt{def:panel-law-class}\), \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) assigns the spacing rate
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}=T^{-q}.
\tag{13}
\]
The same assignment applies algebraically under the separately stated fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition.  Substituting (13) directly into (5) gives, without a logarithmic relaxation,
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\tag{14}
\]
Thus, with \(A_{\mathrm{iid}}:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\), the definition of \(R_\star\) yields the exact identity
\[
R_\star=A_{\mathrm{iid}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{15}
\]

We now connect (12) and (15) to the statistical experiment, rather than treating (15) as comparator algebra only.  Fix a nonempty donor-envelope interior-compatible class, so \(B>D^2\), and take a joint-growth array satisfying the limit conditions in \(\texttt{thm:sharp-joint-frontier}\) and \(\texttt{thm:honest-length-frontier}\).  The beta-mixing part of \(\texttt{thm:sharp-joint-frontier}\) identifies the conditional minimax mean-squared-error order as \(R_{\star,\beta}\), and its independent-calendar corollary identifies that order as \(R_\star\) over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger,\mathrm{iid}}(\lambda)\).  Equations (12) and (15), valid eventually because \(T\to\infty\), therefore turn these respective orders into
\[
A_\beta\vee N^{-\kappa}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
A_{\mathrm{iid}}\vee N^{-\kappa},
\tag{16}
\]
where \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\) by \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\).  Likewise, \(\texttt{thm:honest-length-frontier}\) identifies the optimal uniformly honest expected-length orders as the square roots of the two rates, giving the two square-root expressions in the claim.

Let \(A\) denote either positive quantity \(A_\beta\) or \(A_{\mathrm{iid}}\), as appropriate.  In (16), the donor term is asymptotically negligible precisely when
\[
N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\tag{17}
\]
and is asymptotically dominant precisely when
\[
A=o(N^{-\kappa}).
\tag{18}
\]
Taking square roots preserves both little-order comparisons, so the same regions govern the honest-length rates.  Since \(A>0\) and \(\kappa>0\), the boundary relation \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\) is equivalent, after applying the decreasing map \(x\mapsto x^{-1/\kappa}\) and absorbing fixed comparison constants, to
\[
N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\tag{19}
\]
This proves both phase diagrams.

At \(B=D^2\), the boundary clauses of \(\texttt{thm:sharp-joint-frontier}\) and \(\texttt{thm:honest-length-frontier}\) retain the displayed upper rates and exact conditional coverage but lower-bound only the respective non-donor channel maxima.  Hence (17)--(19) cannot be promoted to a sharp donor phase at equality.  The same theorems state that \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class, so no minimax phase is asserted there.  These case distinctions use exactly the compatibility and limit conditions of the dependent statistical results.

Finally, the two spacing definitions give the exact ratio
\[
\frac{R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}}{R_{\mathrm{sp}}}
=\{\log(T\vee2)\}^{2\lambda/d},
\tag{20}
\]
which proves the stated dependence elbow: the independent-calendar subclass removes the logarithmic factor and changes no other active channel.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\) states
\[
X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}.
\tag{21}
\]
Thus the historical regression coordinate is observed without a measurement-error convolution, so no inversion of such a convolution is required.  Inspection of the exhaustive maxima defining \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and \(R_\star\) in \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) then shows that neither contains a deconvolution component or a separate moving-Gram component.  The same definition sets \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  If \(\lambda>1\), then \(\kappa=1\), and consequently
\[
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}=N^{-1}.
\]
All assertions follow.
